governance_framework.legal_basis: Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991)
governance_framework.history: Originally an agricultural barrio of Mangaldan referred to as balon baley ("new town"), Mapandan was first established as an independent pueblo pursuant to Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, promulgated by Governor General Emilio Bravo on December 28, 1887. Following population and fiscal losses caused by an epidemic in 1905 that temporarily reverted Mapandan to Mangaldan's jurisdiction, the municipality was re-established under American civil administration through Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith in 1909.
governance_framework.legislative_body: Sangguniang Bayan ng Mapandan — unicameral local legislative council presided by the Municipal Vice Mayor, composed of elected councilors and ex-officio representatives from the Liga ng mga Barangay and the Sangguniang Kabataan Federation.
governance_framework.district: Third Congressional District, Province of Pangasinan

legislative_process.title: Filing
legislative_process.description: A proposed ordinance is filed with the Sangguniang Bayan for consideration.

legislative_process.title: First Reading
legislative_process.description: Initial reading and referral to the relevant committee for review.

legislative_process.title: Committee Hearing
legislative_process.description: The committee holds hearings and deliberates on the proposal.

legislative_process.title: Committee Report
legislative_process.description: Findings and recommendations are submitted back to the full council.

legislative_process.title: Second Reading
legislative_process.description: Detailed floor discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance.

legislative_process.title: Third & Final Reading
legislative_process.description: Final vote by the Sangguniang Bayan.

legislative_process.title: Mayor's Approval
legislative_process.description: The Municipal Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance.

legislative_process.title: Provincial Review
legislative_process.description: Submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Pangasinan for legal review under Sections 56 and 57 of R.A. 7160.

legislative_process.title: Posting & Effect
legislative_process.description: The approved ordinance is posted publicly and takes effect across all 15 constituent barangays.

database_schema.description: A structured schema for digital archival of legislative enactments, ensuring long-term data integrity and system interoperability.

fields.name: Document_ID
fields.definition: Unique system identifier: enactment type, year, and sequence

fields.name: Issuing_Body
fields.definition: Legislative or executive entity issuing the measure

fields.name: Document_Number
fields.definition: Official legislative designation and series number

fields.name: Primary_Title
fields.definition: Complete statutory title of the enactment
fields.example: An Ordinance Providing for Ecological Solid Waste Management...

fields.name: Date_Enacted_SB
fields.definition: Date of final reading and passage by local council

fields.name: SP_Review_Date
fields.definition: Date of approval by Sangguniang Panlalawigan

fields.name: Fiscal_Value_PHP
fields.definition: Monetary value or loan amount authorized

fields.name: Verification_Status
fields.definition: Whether the record was confirmed against the full source certification page or derived from title/URL only

procedures: A dual-indexing mechanism links every municipal enactment ID directly to its corresponding Sangguniang Panlalawigan review resolution, preserving the complete chain of legal validity under the Local Government Code.

The digital repository organizes files using a categorical taxonomy: Fiscal & Budgetary Enactments; Personnel & Administrative Restructuring; Regulatory & Revenue Codes; Public Health, Safety, & Welfare; Land Use & Zoning; and Territorial & Boundary Decrees.

Physical archives at the Sangguniang Bayan Secretariat undergo OCR scanning into text-searchable PDF/A digital records, indexed alongside structured metadata for public legal research and ARTA compliance.

precedent.summary: When Vice Mayor Baltazar Aquino assumed the mayoralty, the highest-ranking Sangguniang Bayan member elevated to Vice Mayor, opening a legislative seat. The Supreme Court ruled that the replacement had to come from the same political party as the vacating member, a precedent that continues to guide multi-tier local successions nationwide under Sections 44 and 45 of the Local Government Code.
